You don't actually want the Ferrari. You want how people look at you when you're in it.

Ask yourself why you want anything enough times and it stops being about the object. It becomes about a feeling you don't currently have — and about being seen a certain way by people whose opinion you've never admitted matters to you. Most people get embarrassed the second they realize this. They shouldn't. Naming the real want is the only way to actually get free of it.

They bred salmon for twenty generations on a farm. Not one of them had ever swum upstream.

Scientists said it was impossible — release them in a wild river and they'd simply drown, because the instinct had never been used. So a man released them anyway, into a flooded river in the middle of the desert. Most of them did start to drown. And then, mid-current, something switched on, and they swam upstream anyway. Twenty generations later, the instinct was still there, waiting.

Whatever's in your bloodline is still in you too. It's just waiting for the flood.

An Italian baby, orphaned within weeks, raised entirely by a Japanese family. Never left Japan. Never heard another language. Never met another Italian.

He spoke perfect Japanese, followed every custom, lived every day as Japanese as anyone in the room. Except when he got excited. Then his hands started moving, wildly, completely against Japanese custom — exactly the way an Italian talks. Nobody taught him that. Nobody could have.

Some things aren't learned. They're carried.

Most of the wealthiest people he knows have never once heard the phrase "law of attraction."

Ask them and they'll say they've never read the book, never studied a formula, never used the word manifesting in their life. But listen to how they actually talk: I believe I'm going to succeed. I see myself already in possession of it. They're running the exact formula, word for word, without ever learning its name — because they built it themselves through trial and error, or inherited it from someone who did.

The technique was never the secret. Believing it was already true was.
